title: The City That Paid for Rat Tails

beats.text: In nineteen oh two, a city paid people to kill rats, and made the problem worse.
Imagine you're in Hanoi. The French just built shiny new sewers.
To a rat, that's a cozy palace with no cats.
Rats start popping out of fancy toilets.
So the city hires catchers to crawl into the muck.
One June day, they catch over twenty thousand.
Barely a dent. So, a new offer.
One cent per rat. Just bring a tail to city hall.
Nobody wants a mountain of dead rats at the office.
Tails pour in. Then, something strange.
Rats running around town, alive, healthy, and without tails.
How is that possible? Inspectors outside town find rat farms.
You see, it's like paying a kid per page read. Suddenly they love huge letters.
Kill a rat: one cent, once. Snip its tail and let it go: a cent today, and baby rats tomorrow.
The bounty didn't kill rats. It farmed them.
They weren't paying for fewer rats. They were paying for tails.

facts.claim: In 1902 Hanoi's French colonial government ran a rat-killing campaign that made the rat problem worse
The French had just built a new modern sewer system under Hanoi, where rats bred with no predators
Rats came up through toilets into French homes; the campaign was driven by fear of bubonic plague
Vietnamese rat catchers were hired to hunt rats in the sewers, among human waste
On one day in June 1902 over 20,000 rats were killed (20,112 on June 21 per Wikipedia/Atlas; 20,114 per Saigoneer; 'over 20,000 in a single day' per Vann)
The hunt failed to make a dent against rat breeding
A bounty of one cent per rat was offered to anyone who handed a rat tail to the municipal offices / city hall
Tails were asked for because officials did not want thousands of dead rats brought to city hall
Live, healthy rats without tails were seen; hunters cut tails off and let rats go to breed
Health inspectors found rat-breeding farms on the outskirts of Hanoi
Page-reading analogy is an illustrative everyday analogy, not a historical claim

caption:
In 1902, Hanoi paid one cent per rat tail.
So people started farming rats.
What you measure is what you get.
